permissions.inquiries.read_assigned: Read queue/detail/history for inquiries assigned to the actor as manager or engineer; contact values remain redacted without inquiries.contacts.read.
permissions.inquiries.read_all: Read all inquiry queue/detail/history including unassigned inquiries; contact values remain redacted without inquiries.contacts.read.
permissions.inquiries.contacts.read: Reveal submitted contact snapshots only together with read_assigned or read_all scope.
permissions.inquiries.assign_manager: Assign or replace the manager; clearing an assignment is not supported. Requires read scope and target ACTIVE staff with inquiries.read_assigned or inquiries.read_all.
permissions.inquiries.assign_engineer: Assign or replace the engineer; clearing an assignment is not supported. Requires read scope and target ACTIVE staff with inquiries.read_assigned or inquiries.read_all.
permissions.inquiries.transition: Perform only the approved staff lifecycle transitions or set the current stage due date; requires read scope and transition preconditions.
permissions.inquiries.comment: Append internal-only comments; requires read scope.
permissions.inquiries.documents.read: Read attachment metadata and security state; requires read scope.
permissions.inquiries.documents.download: Download only an authorized CLEAN source document; also requires inquiries.documents.read and read scope.

rules: Public inquiry creation has no staff permission and cannot read, enumerate, update or transition an inquiry.
Knowledge of inquiry UUID or publicReference never grants staff or customer access.
The anonymous upload capability is bound to one inquiry and permits only creating, uploading or cancelling its attachments; it grants no read/status/download access.
Contact PII requires an explicit contact permission in addition to inquiry visibility.
Attachment metadata and byte access are separate permissions; byte access additionally requires CLEAN state and domain policy authorization.
No permission is automatically added to any role. Owner approval and ordinary R1-002 RBAC administration are required to grant codes.
